distributionSurfaces.description: Vite application JavaScript, CSS, fonts, workers, and repository-owned WebAssembly deployed to Cloudflare Pages.
Versioned optional runtimes fetched from assets.soundscaper.org rather than bundled into Pages.
The built web application copied into each Electron product.
FFmpeg and translation runtime assets staged beside the Electron renderer.
Electron, embedded Chromium and Node.js, and the repository-owned main/preload process code.
Public desktop packages, notices, checksums, and corresponding-source archives.

vendoredHeaders.rationale: The SPA format builders the native audio backend needs are static inline functions in the headers, so dlopen cannot reach them. Only headers are checked in; the library is resolved at runtime and never shipped.

releaseGates.blocker: No versioned web route or web artifact currently delivers THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md with the deployed application and optional runtimes.
The current manifest identifies FFmpeg and ffmpeg.wasm archives but does not inventory and pin complete corresponding source for every enabled library in the binary.
No distribution-specific, jurisdiction-specific patent review is recorded for the enabled codec set.

futureDistributionGates.blocker: The current Utility Gain conformance package is repository-owned application code in the closed release catalog; it does not admit an externally authored or non-repository-owned package or satisfy that package's inventory, source, notice, and review duties.

nativeFormatPolicies.upstreamLicensing: FFmpeg GPL build with the thirteen enabled external libraries pinned by the ffmpeg register
nativeFormatPolicies.agplCompatibilityDirection: GPL-2.0-or-later build combines into this AGPL-3.0-only work under the existing runtime provenance row.
nativeFormatPolicies.redistribution: A native FFmpeg helper binary may not ship until the two blocked ffmpeg release gates clear for exactly this enabled set; the set does not grow because a native build makes growth easy.
nativeFormatPolicies.blocker: ffmpeg-enabled-library-corresponding-source and ffmpeg-enabled-codec-patent-review are blocked; a native helper binary inherits both gates unchanged.

nativeFormatPolicies.upstreamLicensing: Platform encoder/decoder services (NVENC, Quick Sync, VideoToolbox, VAAPI) reached through their platform interfaces
nativeFormatPolicies.agplCompatibilityDirection: System-service linkage is used, not combined source; no license flows into the work.
nativeFormatPolicies.redistribution: Nothing is redistributed, but enablement is a per-codec, per-jurisdiction patent question first and a performance feature second.
nativeFormatPolicies.blocker: No jurisdiction-specific patent review is recorded for any hardware-accelerated codec path; enablement waits on the native-codecs gate.

nativeFormatPolicies.upstreamLicensing: Per-format: long-GOP, 10-bit/HDR, image-sequence, alpha-master, and mezzanine codecs each carry their own license and patent posture
nativeFormatPolicies.agplCompatibilityDirection: Reviewed per format before any build flag or helper capability names it.
nativeFormatPolicies.redistribution: No such codec ships until its own row records the license inventory, corresponding-source disposition, and patent review.
nativeFormatPolicies.blocker: No per-format inventory exists; every milestone-5B decode/encode tier lands its own row against the native-codecs gate before it is buildable.

nativeFormatPolicies.upstreamLicensing: FFmpeg's HEVC and AV1 decoders under the pinned GPL build; HEVC is additionally encumbered by the MPEG LA, Access Advance, and Velos Media pools, while AV1 is covered by the Alliance for Open Media patent licence
nativeFormatPolicies.agplCompatibilityDirection: Decoder source combines into this AGPL-3.0-only work exactly as the rest of the pinned FFmpeg build does; the patent position is separate from and unaffected by the copyright licence.
nativeFormatPolicies.redistribution: Neither decoder ships until this row records the per-pool, per-jurisdiction patent review and the corresponding-source disposition for the enlarged enabled set.
nativeFormatPolicies.blocker: No HEVC pool review and no AV1 patent-licence review are recorded, and enabling either decoder enlarges the FFmpeg enabled set that ffmpeg-enabled-library-corresponding-source and ffmpeg-enabled-codec-patent-review already gate.

nativeFormatPolicies.upstreamLicensing: PNG and TIFF through the pinned FFmpeg build's own decoders; OpenEXR through FFmpeg's EXR decoder, with any libopenexr linkage carrying the OpenEXR BSD-3-Clause licence
nativeFormatPolicies.agplCompatibilityDirection: Permissive still-image code combines into this AGPL-3.0-only work; the FFmpeg-internal decoders inherit the existing GPL build posture.
nativeFormatPolicies.redistribution: Image-sequence decode and encode do not ship until this row records which decoder implementation is enabled, its notices, and its corresponding-source disposition.
nativeFormatPolicies.blocker: No decision is recorded on whether image-sequence support uses FFmpeg-internal decoders or external libraries, so neither the notices nor the corresponding-source inventory can be written.

nativeFormatPolicies.upstreamLicensing: QuickTime/MOV, SMPTE MXF, and Matroska muxers and demuxers from the pinned FFmpeg build; the Matroska specification is BSD-licensed and MXF is an open SMPTE standard
nativeFormatPolicies.agplCompatibilityDirection: Container code combines into this AGPL-3.0-only work under the existing FFmpeg runtime provenance row; no separate licence flows in.
nativeFormatPolicies.redistribution: These containers do not ship until the enlarged FFmpeg enabled set clears its corresponding-source gate, because enabling a muxer enlarges exactly that set.
nativeFormatPolicies.blocker: Enabling the MOV, MXF, and Matroska muxers enlarges the FFmpeg enabled set that ffmpeg-enabled-library-corresponding-source gates, and no notices or corresponding-source inventory has been written for the enlarged set.

refusedLocalModels.reason: Verbatim transcription with filler-word timings is exactly the 7A-2 use case, but the weights forbid commercial use. Parakeet timing plus a filler lexicon replaces it.
The common forced aligner and every ONNX re-export inherit non-commercial terms from the upstream multilingual speech project. English realignment uses wav2vec2-base-960h instead.
End-to-end diarization with non-commercial weights; ONNX conversions inherit the restriction. The segmentation and embedding pipeline replaces it.
The original Canary release is non-commercial. The later flash and v2 refreshes are CC-BY-4.0 but add nothing over Parakeet for these products.
The madmom code is permissive but its trained models are non-commercial, which contaminates anything loading them. Beat This provides MIT beat and downbeat weights.

Separation weights are non-commercial despite permissive code.
The additional conditions forbid deployment that competes with the vendor and restrict onward redistribution, so it is not redistributable here. Silero VAD replaces it.
The pretrained models are non-commercial. The AGPL code alone would be compatible with this product, but the weights are not redistributable.
No community checkpoint carries per-file terms and training-data provenance is undocumented, so no record can be completed.
Checkpoints are published only through shared-drive links with no stable source, and the hosting repository has a history of per-model licence exceptions. PANNs CNN14 covers the same tagging need.
